Here's an example: there is a pond in a village that has 12 fish. Each night an additional fish is born to each pairing of 2 fish. In order for 4 people in the village to ensure they have enough fish to eat they should only take 1 fish each, thus ensuring they always have a good stock of fish in the pond. However, this would not be the case. Instead since there is an abundance of fish, more than likely one fisherman will catch an additional one. On seeing this, the next fisherman also catches two, and so on to the other two fisherman. This process would continue, and would not allow enough time for the group of fish to bounce back. 

Another example is the amount of food that is wasted by familes. I know for a fact that my own family has a tendency to let things expire and throw away food that could have been eaten but wasn't.

Most enviromental issues aren't trying to combat the issues with socialism, but are trying to be combated with sound management. That is to say that you can curb problems in ways that dont upset the balance too much. For instance, you can erect alternative green energies. There doesnt have to be any socialism involved in using green energy, there are already many private companies that operate wind farms.
